breaks.observed: VERIFIED: both passes return unknownStorage=true and items=[]; port.release() is never called; siblings stay [release_pending, attempt_count 0] and [reserved, attempt_count 0]; the corrupt row keeps attempt_count 0 so it sorts first (`ORDER BY attempt_count, created_at_ms`) on every pass. Root cause INFERRED from src/analysis/runJournal.ts recover(): `for (const row of rows) { const entry = decode(row); ... }` — the first decode() throw aborts the whole batch before recoverOne() runs for any later row, and recoverAnalysisJournals() swallows it as unknownStorage. syncRuntime treats unknownStorage as pendingRecovery (backoff) but never gets past the row. Impact: device-side release of orphaned reserved permits never happens; access_state() counts them as `reserved` (free-rating allowance shows used/reserved) until the server-side 24h stale-permit sweep. No credit is consumed and the corrupt row itself is correctly left untouched.

Then call recoverAnalysisJournals(db, scope, port) twice.

BASELINE (VERIFIED): `cd apps/mobile && npx jest --silent __tests__/syncIntegrity.integration.test.ts` exit 0, 1 suite, 31 passed/0 failed/0 skipped.

ATTACK RUN (VERIFIED): `cd apps/mobile && npm ci && npx jest __tests__/adv` exit 1 — 2 suites, 13 tests: 12 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped (artifact attack_all_run7.log). The single failure is the confirmed break above. Earlier runs 1–6 (attack_outbox_run1.log) failed only on harness/expectation defects that I corrected (SQL NUL literal, `last_error` stores the human message not the code, `remaining` counts exhausted rows, outbox status name is 'queued', all-digit ids made toUpperCase a no-op, local_capture UNIQUE(owner_key, uri), runJournal.commit requires the raw transaction) — none of those were product failures.
FULL MOBILE SUITE (VERIFIED): `cd apps/mobile && npx jest --silent` exit 1 — 316 suites (314 passed, 1 failed = the new reproducing adversary test, 1 skipped pre-existing suite unrelated to this branch), 6062 tests: 6060 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (mobile_full_jest.log). `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 (after `npm ci`; before it, 20 pre-existing errors from a missing @sentry/react-native install in the snapshot, none in the new files). Root `npx eslint <both new files>` exit 0; `npx prettier --check apps/mobile/__tests__/adv/*.adv.test.ts` exit 0.

ATTACKS THAT DID NOT BREAK ANYTHING (all VERIFIED passing, command `cd apps/mobile && npx jest __tests__/adv/syncOutboxPersistence.adv.test.ts` exit 0, 10/10 passed; and the two passing probes in runJournalPersistence.adv.test.ts):
1. Process death after server acceptance but before the receipt write, file-backed SQLite reopened as a relaunch → same byte-identical payload replayed, exactly one receipt, no duplicate local_shot.
2. Account switch A→B→A between two accepted receipts of one batch → DataOwnerChangedError fences the remaining writes; only pre-switch receipts committed; B's tables untouched; A's remaining rows replay after switching back.
3. Corrupt shot.sync payload (NUL/truncation) for a real local_shot → never a receipt, never empty history (listShots still shows both ratings), row exhausts alone at OUTBOX_MAX_ATTEMPTS=8 while the sibling syncs, survives relaunch, `remaining` keeps reporting the exhausted row (informational; runtime backoff keys on `failed`, INFERRED from syncRuntime.ts).
4. Corrupt session.create parent with two dependent shots + finalize → shots rejected with shot.session_not_found trigger exactly one reconstructed parent from local_session; second drain delivers create→shots→finalize; corrupt parent keeps failing alone (attempts 2), no receipt fabricated.
5. Real createTransport with a 20 000 ms fetch timeout then a late server acceptance → AbortController aborted, row kept with attempts 0 (408 is transient), the late response never writes a receipt, retry resends the byte-identical body.
6. HTTP 429 mid-flush after the parent session was created and finalized → delivered parents deleted, shots kept with attempts 0 and the 429 message in last_error, second drain never re-creates the session.
7. Double saveSession / double saveAnalysis / double finishSession (6 outbox rows) → identical duplicates deduplicated in dependency order, one syncShots call, one receipt, one local_session, one local_shot.
8. Mixed acknowledgement at the OUTBOX_MAX_ATTEMPTS boundary → sibling receipt committed, rejected row exhausted at exactly 8 attempts and never resent; both ratings remain in local history.
9. SQLite COMMIT acknowledgement lost after the physical receipt/delete commit of the first of two accepted entries → committed receipt kept, its row gone, sibling row untouched with attempts 0, second drain resends only the sibling, final state exactly two receipts / zero rows.
10. Server ack that renames a submitted id (case-changed hex UUID) via the real HTTP transport → decodeSyncVerdicts rejects it (sync.invalid_acknowledgement), zero receipts, attempts stay 0, status 'queued', a correct ack later syncs both.
11a. Corrupt journal row isolation → unknownStorage=true, the corrupt row is byte-identical afterwards, its permit is never released (correct HOLD behaviour).
12. Process death inside the result/journal/outbox commit transaction (failStatementOnce on INSERT INTO outbox) → zero local_shot/outbox/sync_receipt rows, journal still `reserved`; then a lost COMMIT ack after the physical commit → local_shot+outbox+committed journal all present together, recovery releases nothing, re-running commit is idempotent (still one outbox row).

NOT_YET_VERIFIABLE (needs Mac/device; not guessed): real iOS SQLite/op-sqlite behaviour of these same probes and true app-kill-during-transaction on device — `scripts/mac-full-verify.sh` on the M4 runner (coordinator-owned; I did not use --remote) plus `cd apps/mobile/ios && bundle exec pod install && xcodebuild test -workspace PickleSensei.xcworkspace -scheme PickleSensei -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16'`. Server-side stale-permit sweep interaction with break #1 (24h pg_cron sweep, INFERRED from supabase/migrations/20260901000000_permit_reservation_race.sql) would need `./supabase/tests/run_rls_tests.sh` against a local Postgres plus a live permit fixture — not run here.

Note for the coordinator on break #1: the existing pin `__tests__/originalAnalysisRetry.test.ts` (unknownStorage=true when the whole SELECT fails) does not cover a single undecodable row among valid rows; the design comment says a failed *storage version* is UNKNOWN, which is consistent, but a single row poisoning the whole batch — and never advancing because attempt_count is only bumped inside recoverOne — is head-of-line blocking of permit recovery for the lifetime of that row.
